books.section: Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution (ratified December 6, 1865)

stimulus.text:
“Section 1. Neither slavery nor involuntary servitude, except as a punishment for crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted, shall exist within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction. Section 2. Congress shall have power to enforce this article by appropriate legislation.”

—Thirteenth Amendment, ratified December 6, 1865
stimulus.source_note: Thirteenth Amendment, ratified December 6, 1865. Public domain. Wording verified against the Constitution Annotated (Congress.gov).

rationales.A: Background: freeing only rebel states was the Proclamation’s limit, and this amendment goes past it.
rationales.B: The Proclamation freed enslaved people only in rebel territory, leaving slavery standing in Kentucky and Delaware. The amendment bans slavery everywhere in the United States, closing the gap the Proclamation left.
rationales.C: Background: the vote came with the Fifteenth Amendment, five years later.
rationales.D: Background: an amendment needs Congress and the states, and Lincoln’s signature was not even required.
rationales.general:
1. The Proclamation was a war measure, and it reached only states in rebellion.
2. Background: slavery still stood in the loyal border states, Kentucky and Delaware.
3. The amendment’s words cover the whole country: “shall exist within the United States, or any place subject to their jurisdiction.”
4. So the amendment finished what the Proclamation started.
Remember: a proclamation frees people where the war reaches; an amendment frees them everywhere.
